News Radar — 军事新闻

2026-07-18 · Window: 24h · Items: 59 · Generated: 2026-07-18 04:14 UTC

Editor's Brief

The last 24 hours have been dominated by a sharp escalation in U.S.-Iran hostilities, with mutual infrastructure strikes and a renewed blockade severely disrupting Strait of Hormuz traffic. Concurrently, a new GAO report reveals major delays and cost overruns in the U.S. hypersonic missile program, while China's military assertiveness in the South China Sea and Indo-Pacific continues to draw countermeasures from regional partners. AI is emerging as a new flashpoint in information warfare.

  • U.S.-Iran strikes escalate: The sixth consecutive night of U.S. strikes in Iran targeted bridges and military infrastructure, while Iran retaliated. A U.S. blockade of Iranian ports led to a tanker being disabled by Hellfire missiles. Strait of Hormuz traffic has plunged as risk appetite evaporates. Mutual strikes have pushed oil prices to a weekly gain.
  • Hypersonic missile program in trouble: The GAO found the Navy is two years behind schedule on installing hypersonic missiles on Zumwalt-class destroyers, with Lockheed Martin struggling to scale production. Breaking Defense reports a lack of unified strategy may waste billions. Meanwhile, the USS Zumwalt is finally set to return to fleet after a long upgrade. TWZ
  • Air Force ramps up missile production: The U.S. Air Force is expanding procurement of stealthy cruise and anti-ship missiles (JASSM/LRASM) from 16,710 to 23,095 units to counter China's naval threat. USNI News
  • Australia unveils fake Chinese tank: The Australian Army displayed an Abrams tank disguised as a PLA Type 99 to enhance realism in exercises against its primary adversary. TWZ
  • China’s SLBM launch: France confirms it had advance notice of China’s submarine-launched ballistic missile test, viewed as a demonstration of nuclear deterrence. Naval News
  • AI propaganda war: Chinese state media used AI-generated video depicting Filipinos as monkeys, prompting condemnation from Manila. RFI

Watch next: The dual shipping lane threats in the Middle East could further destabilize global oil markets. The U.S. hypersonic missile timeline will be scrutinized in upcoming congressional hearings. China’s response to Australia-Vanuatu base denial and continued South China Sea patrols will shape regional dynamics.

冲突局势 · 12 items

U.S.-Iran tensions have exploded into open conflict over the Strait of Hormuz, with mutual infrastructure strikes and a blockade causing a dramatic drop in maritime traffic. The Pope has appealed to Russia to restore the grain agreement, while analysts warn of an all-out Middle East war.

  • U.S.-Iran mutual strikes: The U.S. military hit 'dozens of Iranian targets' overnight, including bridges, while Iran retaliated. Honolulu Star-Advertiser
  • Strait of Hormuz traffic plunges: Renewed tensions reverse normalization; transits hit a low as risk appetite falls. Anadolu Ajansı and Yeni Safak
  • Oil prices rise: Dual Middle East shipping lane threats push oil to a weekly gain. Baird Maritime
  • Pope appeals on grain deal: Francis calls on 'his Russian brothers' to restore the Black Sea grain agreement. AsiaNews
  • Mearsheimer warns of all-out war: Analyst John Mearsheimer discusses the potential for a wider Middle East war and Trump’s policy on Russia. The Singju Post

Bottom line: The Strait of Hormuz is now a flashpoint for a broader U.S.-Iran war, with economic and humanitarian repercussions that could reshape global energy flows and food security.

国际安全 · 30 items

The U.S. hypersonic missile program faces mounting criticism after a GAO report revealed the Navy is two years behind schedule on Zumwalt upgrades and Lockheed Martin is struggling to scale production. The Air Force is compensating by rapidly expanding procurement of stealthy cruise and anti-ship missiles, while new industrial investments emerge for drone ships and missile defense.

  • GAO warns of wasted money: The Navy and Army lack a unified hypersonic strategy, risking billions. Breaking Defense and DefenseScoop
  • USS Zumwalt returns after delay: The destroyer is set to rejoin the fleet with hypersonic missiles, but power plant issues contributed to the delay. TWZ and Defense News
  • Air Force boosts missile production: Contracts for JASSM and LRASM expanded to 23,095 units to counter China. USNI News and Crypto Briefing
  • Drone ship maker goes big: Saronic announces a $3B shipyard in Texas capable of building 850-foot vessels. TWZ
  • Harpoon missile at 50: The Cold War-era anti-ship missile refuses to retire as a key ship-killer. 19FortyFive

Bottom line: The U.S. is racing to modernize its missile arsenal amid industrial bottlenecks, but the hypersonic program's delays and lack of coordination may leave critical capability gaps for years.

The Strait of Hormuz crisis dominates naval headlines, with the U.S. disabling a tanker during its blockade and transits at historic lows. Meanwhile, the Spanish Navy takes leadership of NATO's Atlantic task force, and Japan-Vietnam defense cooperation deepens with a fast landing craft project.

  • Golden Defender missile monitor ship: Hanwha Philly Shipyard to build a new missile-range instrumentation vessel for the Golden Dome program. USNI News and Breaking Defense
  • RIMPAC underway: The at-sea phase of RIMPAC 2026 is ongoing; Singapore Navy frigate RSS Steadfast fired an Aster missile. USNI News
  • Spanish Navy leads NATO Atlantic task force: Five Spanish ships and eight allied vessels will patrol the North Atlantic until June 2027. USNI News
  • Japan-Vietnam landing craft: Tokyo and Hanoi agree to jointly develop fast landing craft, marking deeper defense-industrial ties. Naval News

Bottom line: The U.S. Navy is stretched between a hot war in the Middle East and a deterrence posture in the Indo-Pacific, while allies step up in both theaters.
